A memo from CEO Suzanne Scott and president Jay Wallace said Fox received a complaint from a former employee's attorney alleging willful sexual misconduct in the workplace years earlier, retained an outside law firm, and terminated Henry based on investigative findings. Henry's lawyer said he denied the allegations.

21st Century Fox said in April 2017 that, after a thorough and careful review of allegations against him, it and O'Reilly had agreed he would not return to Fox News. The New York Times reported that he or the company had paid about $13 million to settle claims by five women, and in October 2017 a further $32 million settlement with a Fox News analyst. Fox said it knew a harassment suit had been threatened and that O'Reilly told it he had settled personally on confidential terms. The settlements are not admissions; O'Reilly denied wrongdoing and called the claims unfounded.

The New Yorker said in December 2017 that it had learned Lizza engaged in what it believed was improper sexual conduct and that, after reviewing the matter, it had severed ties with him. Lizza denied wrongdoing, objected to the characterization of a relationship with a woman he had dated, and called the decision a terrible mistake made without a full investigation.
note: Opened sources do not show the woman was a colleague; the misconduct category covers conduct toward colleagues.

category: Breach of morals clause (relationships with subordinates)
outcome: Show suspended; jury verdict for PBS
summary: PBS suspended Smiley's show in December 2017 after an outside investigation. In March 2020 a Washington, D.C. jury found he had violated the morals clause in his PBS contract and awarded PBS about $1.49 million. The investigation report described allegations from women that they had relationships with Smiley while they were his subordinates. Smiley denied the accusations.
note: Jury (Mar 2020) found TS Media breached the PBS morals clause; judgment of $2.6M (Aug 2020); an appeal was filed with no outcome found. He admitted dating women who worked for his own company. The employer question is unresolved.

outcome: Suspended two months; removed from beat
summary: The New York Times suspended Thrush in November 2017 over allegations involving younger female journalists from his time at Politico. In December executive editor Dean Baquet said the investigation found Thrush had behaved in ways the paper did not condone and had acted offensively, but did not deserve to be fired; he was given workplace-conduct training and moved to a new beat.
note: Employer said he 'acted offensively' but did not say the conduct was sexual; conduct predates his NYT job.

summary: CBC fired Ghomeshi in October 2014. CBC executive Heather Conway said the broadcaster had seen evidence that he caused physical injury to a woman, calling it a fundamental breach of CBC's standard of acceptable conduct for any employee. Ghomeshi denied non-consensual conduct and was later acquitted of related criminal charges.
note: CBC cited physical injury to a woman; no opened source links it to the workplace or a colleague; acquitted at criminal trial.

category: Inappropriate sexual language; unwanted physical contact
summary: An investigation by law firm Lewis Silkin, commissioned by MasterChef producer Banijay UK and published in July 2025, substantiated 45 of 83 allegations against Wallace, mostly inappropriate sexual language and humour, being in a state of undress, and one instance of unwelcome physical contact. Banijay said his return to MasterChef was untenable, and the BBC said it had no plans to work with him. Wallace apologised for some language but said he had been cleared of the most serious accusations.
note: Banijay upheld 45 allegations, but whether he was an employee or engaged via a company is unconfirmed.

summary: Schofield left ITV's This Morning in May 2023 and admitted he had lied about a consensual relationship with a younger male colleague. ITV chief executive Carolyn McCall said in a letter that both people had repeatedly denied rumours of a relationship when questioned, and ITV commissioned a barrister-led external review.
note: The ITV external review found the relationship was repeatedly denied until his May 2023 admission. ITV earlier said he 'lied'. No ITV statement names a policy breach (ITV only later introduced a relationships policy). He is a presenter, so the 'prominent employee' bar needs confirmed or better, and this is only 'acknowledged'.

summary: Minnesota Public Radio terminated its contracts with Keillor and his companies in November 2017, citing allegations of inappropriate behavior with an individual who worked with him. Keillor disputed MPR's account. MPR and Keillor later reached a settlement in 2018.
note: Contractor; MPR did not explicitly call the behaviour sexual.

outcome: Contract not renewed (Jun 2017, before allegations public)
summary: New York magazine reported in December 2017 that several former colleagues alleged harassment and bullying by Hockenberry. NYPR said his contract had not been renewed in mid-2017. Hockenberry apologized for some behavior.
note: No employer finding; contract had lapsed.

summary: New York Public Radio fired Lopate in December 2017 after an outside-counsel investigation, saying he violated its standards for an inclusive, appropriate and respectful workplace. WNYC said he had earlier been warned over inappropriate remarks to staff. Lopate denied wrongdoing.
note: Fired over workplace standards; employer did not say the conduct was sexual.

summary: New York Public Radio fired Schwartz in December 2017 after an outside-counsel investigation, citing violations of its workplace standards following multiple complaints. Earlier reporting described an allegation of inappropriate touching and a sexual comment.
note: Fired over workplace standards; employer did not say the conduct was sexual.

summary: Matthews announced his retirement on air in March 2020 after a GQ column described comments he made to a guest. He apologized, saying compliments on women's appearance were never OK. Reporting said a 2017 separation payment followed comments to a subordinate.
note: Apologised, but no employer finding.

summary: Fox News parted ways with Bolling in September 2017 after HuffPost reported he sent explicit images to colleagues. Fox said outside counsel conducted a privileged review and that the split was amicable. Bolling denied the allegations.
note: Outside review was privileged; departure called amicable.

summary: Franklin resigned as director of the Cleveland Museum of Art in October 2013, and the museum first cited personal reasons. After Cleveland Scene reported that an affair lay behind the resignation, board chairman R. Steven Kestner said the board had confirmed in early October that a dating relationship had existed with a former employee during and after her employment. Kestner said Franklin had denied the relationship when questioned earlier in 2013, and that an earlier attorney inquiry found no credible evidence.

outcome: Fined $50,000; retained; resigned Jan 2011 (board and Levy said unrelated)
summary: In May 2010 the Beth Israel Deaconess board fined CEO Paul Levy $50,000 over a personal relationship with a former employee, calling it a serious lapse of judgment, and kept him in his post. Levy said he had made an error in judgment and that the board acted appropriately. At the hospital's request, the Massachusetts attorney general reviewed the matter, found no misuse of charitable funds and called the fine sufficient. Levy resigned in January 2011, and both he and the board said the departure was unrelated.

outcome: Departed; board said he is no longer employed
summary: The New York Times reported in January 2020 that Helmer had dated and made advances toward women he worked with, including some who reported to him, mostly during his earlier role at the Philadelphia Museum of Art. Days later the Erie Art Museum board said he was no longer employed there, without saying whether he resigned or was fired.
note: Watch: the conduct is at a prior employer, where he was not an executive, and it is mixed with harassment allegations, which belong to the misconduct bar. The NYT original was not found or opened. WHYY opened: the NYT reported he dated subordinates at the PMA, apparently against museum policy. He declined to discuss it and suggested office politics.

outcome: Left firm (described as mutual parting); Gibson Dunn offer withdrawn
summary: Cullerton, a Wachtell litigation partner, left the firm in 2026 after a widely shared video showed him with a junior associate. Bloomberg Law, citing the New York Post, reported that he had been on leave for weeks while the firm investigated the relationship.
note: Watch: a partner is not an executive. Prominent-employee cases need confirmed, adjudicated or settled evidence. The opened Bloomberg excerpt carries no firm statement, and the 'mutual parting' quote is from secondary coverage I did not open. Never name the associate.

summary: Schultz resigned as CEO of Harvard Pilgrim in June 2018. In his letter he acknowledged behavior inconsistent with his and the company's core values and code of conduct. Neither he nor the company specified the conduct.
note: Watch: vague 'personal conduct' departure with no reporting found that ties it to a relationship.

role: Senior Vice President, Booking, NBC News
summary: NBC News said in November 2017 that it had learned Zimmerman engaged in inappropriate conduct with more than one woman at NBCUniversal, in violation of company policy, and that he had been dismissed. NBC did not describe the conduct further. Zimmerman could not be reached for comment at the time.

role: Senior executive producer, Good Morning America (former)
outcome: Lawsuit settled; had left ABC in 2021
summary: A former ABC News producer sued ABC and Corn in 2021, alleging that Corn sexually assaulted her on a 2015 work trip and created a hostile workplace. Corn denied the allegations. ABC said it had investigated her 2021 complaint, and Corn left ABC that year. In October 2023 the parties resolved the case and it was dismissed with prejudice on undisclosed terms; a settlement is not an admission of wrongdoing.
note: Sources conflict on settlement terms and whether he was named; exit date and VP-level title unconfirmed.

outcome: Had already left (Aug 2019); named in derivative suits settled 2021
summary: The New York Times reported in February 2020 that Razek had been accused of inappropriate conduct toward models and employees; Razek called the accusations categorically untrue, misconstrued or taken out of context. Shareholder derivative suits naming him, Leslie Wexner and others were settled in 2021 with L Brands committing $90 million to workplace reforms; the settlement contained no finding against him.
note: Only the NYT did its own reporting; he denies it; L Brands never confirmed the conduct.

category: Sexually explicit video sent to junior colleague
summary: Bloomberg reported in June 2023 that Dell paid a multimillion-dollar settlement to a junior colleague after mistakenly sending her a work video that included sexually explicit content. Goldman said the report contained significant factual errors. Dell did not respond to requests for comment.
note: Single source (Bloomberg); Goldman disputes the report.

summary: The New York Post reported in March 2023 that ESPN fired King after a harassment complaint was brought to human resources. ESPN did not comment, and King described his exit as his own decision.
note: Single NY Post report; no company confirmation.

summary: Media reports in 2023 said ESPN fired Fitting after an HR investigation into complaints that he engaged in inappropriate conduct toward women. He denied some of the allegations.
note: One major outlet (The Athletic/NYT); ESPN confirmed only the departure; he partly denies.

summary: Kroger said in March 2025 that McMullen resigned after an outside-counsel investigation into his personal conduct. The company said the conduct was unrelated to the business and did not involve Kroger associates, but was inconsistent with its Policy on Business Ethics.
note: Vague 'personal conduct' exit; Kroger said no employees were involved; no relationship reported.

summary: Ford said in February 2018 that Nair was leaving after an internal investigation, prompted by an anonymous hotline complaint, found behavior inconsistent with its code of conduct. Ford did not specify the conduct; Nair expressed regret in a statement.
note: Unspecified code-of-conduct breach; nothing ties it to a relationship or sexual conduct.

summary: Visa dismissed McCarthy, its executive vice president of innovation and strategic partnerships, in December 2017, and an internal memo said he had violated company policy. The Wall Street Journal reported that the firing followed an investigation into inappropriate relationships with female Visa employees, which began after the CEO received an anonymous email. Visa did not describe the allegations publicly.

sources.label: Digital Transactions brief citing WSJ, Dec 18, 2017

note: Visa cited a policy violation; WSJ reported relationships with female employees, seen only second-hand; needs a second independent outlet.

summary: Baker resigned as Uber's vice president of product and growth in March 2017 during a company-wide culture investigation. Recode reported, citing anonymous sources, that he had been seen kissing another Uber employee at a company event, and said those sources did not describe harassment. Baker's email to staff cited a desire to move into public service, and Uber gave no reason for the departure.
note: Single anonymous Recode report; Uber never tied it to his exit.
